summary:
Successor to the 2026-10-23 capture, which was made while the nuget.org narrowing pass was still pending. Recorded by fdev (Programme/root) on 2026-10-24. Evidence: FS-GG/FS.GG.Coordination#1026 comments 6385868610 (policy narrowing) and 6386546521 (organization secrets), both supplied by the org/package owner because no public API exposes these surfaces.

Unchanged mechanism: a nuget.org GitHub Trusted Publishing policy matches the owner, repository, workflow file name and, only when set, the environment. It has no ref or branch field. So the package glob is the fence: under a '*' glob, a same-named workflow on any branch can mint a push key for every package the account owns.

State after the 2026-10-24 owner pass (owner-attested, not machine-verified):
- Package owner Paradigma11 has 16 policies. The six retired-producer policies were already deleted, and Callable-Cli-release-publish was already narrowed to FS.GG.Coordination.Cli.
- The 11 remaining '*' policies were narrowed:
  - SDD: FS.GG.SDD.* plus FS.GG.Contracts
  - Rendering: FS.GG.UI*
  - Governance: FS.GG.Governance.*
  - newSDDFullStack: FS.GG.NewSddWorkspace
  - Templates: FS.GG.Templates and FS.GG.Workspace.Template (or FS.GG.*Template*)
  - Game: FS.GG.Game.*
  - Audio: FS.GG.Audio.*
  - Net: FS.GG.Net.*
  - Game skills: FS.GG.Game.Skills
  - Rendering skills: FS.GG.Rendering.Skills
  - FsQuint: FsQuint*
- Only fs-gg-execution-pair-forward-publish (environment execution-pair-forward) matches FS.GG.Execution.*.
- These patterns were derived from the 61 packages Paradigma11 owns on nuget.org.

nuget.org UI constraints observed:
- The glob field takes a single pattern. Exact IDs are chosen separately, in the package picker. A comma list mixing a glob with an exact ID, typed into the glob field, is rejected.
- For one policy (Game), exact-ID entry did not work, and a single prefix glob was used instead.
- Prefer one 'Prefix*' or 'Prefix.*' glob, plus picker entries only where needed.
- Exact IDs block brand-new package IDs until the policy is edited. A producer that adds a package (for example new Templates workspace-provider packs) needs its policy updated first.

Organization Actions secrets (owner-observed, because the PAT gets 403):
- Exactly two exist, FSGG_DISPATCH_APP_ID and FSGG_DISPATCH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, each visible to 11 repositories. Attributing them to the fs-gg-cross-repo-dispatch app is inferred from their names.
- No organization secret carries a NuGet API key. nuget.org publication is OIDC Trusted Publishing only, so no org secret lets a non-forward workflow push FS.GG.Execution.*.
- The 'protection-reader App' named in the Coordination custody decision is a prospective principal, not an installed app.

Limits:
- Policy state, secret visibility and workflow enablement are live owner-controlled facts. Re-read them before relying on the fence.
- The final policy list was not re-pasted after the edit, and ambiguous rows record both acceptable forms.
- This record grants no publication, route enablement or policy change. The execution-pair forward route stays dormant.
title: nuget.org Trusted Publishing fence: per-policy package globs narrowed; only the forward policy matches FS.GG.Execution.*
